source.citation: Chen, D. (2015). Online Retail. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5BW33

numeric_policy: XLSX numeric XML decoded as finite binary64, shortest round-trip decimal string; exact Decimal quantity*GBP_price*100 integer pence; no monetary rounding

selection.policy: SHA256-order complete eligible invoice groups; skip a group if it exceeds remaining row capacity; all selected eligible lines retained; positive sales only

cases.description: Correct the quantity on one sampled invoice line in 2010-12.
Add a staged refund in 2010-12; gross sales remain reusable.
Correct the illustrative GBP conversion for 2010-12 to 1.27 USD.
Reorder identical selected invoice lines from 2010-12; canonical source input remains equal.
A quantity correction in 2011-02 must reach both gross and net branches and later reused briefs.
A one-penny unit-price correction in 2011-05 changes a sampled invoice subtotal.
Add a clearly staged refund in 2011-08; only the net branch and its consumers need revalidation.
Correct the illustrative GBP-to-USD rate in 2011-11 to 1.31; earlier partition evidence stays usable.
Offset two United Kingdom invoice-line subtotals in 2011-02 by one penny; all country aggregates remain equal but source contents change.
Apply a staged refund in 2011-05 and a quantity correction in 2011-11; find their combined cross-run impact.
The illustrative FX source for 2011-08 is unavailable; block dependent claims while preserving other dated reports.
The conversion implementation version is replaced for every saved snapshot; arithmetic is unchanged but old receipts require revalidation.
Reorder the identical selected invoice lines in 2011-05; normalization must preserve source identities and do no new calculations.
Correct one quantity in 2011-11, then reopen the application before selecting evidence and refreshing cross-partition briefs.

limitations: Positive sampled sales, not complete merchant revenue
FX and corrections are staged interventions, not historical incidents
No CustomerID or product descriptions exported
No ticket or refund observations invented; initial refund/ticket sources empty
Gross conversion uses the existing monetary-region contract; the input port named net receives explicitly labeled gross monetary values
